title: Faster strings via BexStr, and a baml.time module with Instant and Duration
lede: BAML's VM now uses BexStr, a V8-inspired string type that replaces std::string::String across the runtime. A new baml.time module ships Instant and Duration with nanosecond granularity and RFC3339 serialization.
highlights: BexStr replaces std::string::String across the VM. Cheap clones, char-indexed string ops.
New baml.time.Instant and baml.time.Duration with nanosecond granularity. RFC3339 canonical form.
Stale field-slot reads raise baml.panics.InvalidFieldAccess instead of crashing the VM.
Builtin definitions now require a throws clause.

breaking.title: Builtin definitions must declare what they throw
breaking.summary: Every builtin in baml_std now needs a throws clause. This affects anyone authoring builtins through the baml_builtins macros or codegen; ordinary user-defined functions are unchanged.
breaking.after: fn read_file(path: string) throws baml.io.IoError -> string
breaking.migration: Add `throws never` for builtins that cannot fail, or `throws <ErrorType>` naming the error you raise. The compiler will reject builtin declarations missing the clause; the entries in baml_builtins2/baml_std/baml/*.baml are the canonical reference.

content.text: The VM used std::string::String for every BAML string, so every clone was a heap allocation plus a memcpy, map-key lookups rehashed from scratch, and concat loops were O(n^2) from repeated clone+push_str. For LLM output processing (JSON parsing, splitting, template rendering) that allocation pressure showed up everywhere.

BexStr is a V8-inspired string type with cheap clone semantics. It also fixes a latent correctness bug: string operations now index by Unicode characters, not bytes. Anything that took an index or length now does the right thing on multi-byte input.

content.code:
let greeting = "😀hello"
- let first = greeting.substring(0, 1)  // old: partial bytes of the emoji
+ let first = greeting.substring(0, 1)  // new: "😀"
- let n = greeting.length              // old: 9 (bytes)
+ let n = greeting.length              // new: 6 (chars)
content.caption: Substring and length switched from byte indexing to char indexing.

content.text: Instant is an absolute point in time with nanosecond granularity. Duration is the span between two Instants. Canonical serialization for Instant is an RFC3339 timestamp, so they round-trip cleanly through prompts and JSON. The language does not currently support operator overloading, so arithmetic is method-based for now, and Instant does not override structural-as-prompt coercion yet.
Hardened VM after the spawn-raced arithmetic work

Follow-up to the specialization changes in 0.11.0-alpha.4340. The specialized int and float arithmetic opcodes are now skipped when either operand reads a captured local or a value derived from one, which closes a class of miscompiles around spawn-raced closures. Plain non-captured arithmetic stays on the fast path.

Out-of-bounds reads against a stale VM field slot now raise a catchable baml.panics.InvalidFieldAccess instead of bubbling up as a Rust panic. Bytecode and execution coverage was added for captured scalar arithmetic, captured float[] element arithmetic, and a deterministic stale field-slot access.

items: Builtin declarations now require a throws clause. See the breaking change above.
$init_test_<file_id> identifiers are path-based instead of using an unstable index, so adding a new file no longer churns every test snapshot.
Fixed the multi-host-call test harness, which had a single slot and broke under parallel tests.
Python SDK test setup uses the project's stable venv instead of spinning up pinned build environments per run.
